mainTopic: In-between cases (a פלגס as a בריה, שיאור dough for a תודה vow), and the opposite rules of פרה אדומה and עגלה ערופה
overview: The גמרא finishes a discussion about the פלגס, an animal past the age of a lamb but not yet a ram. בר פדא says one brings the larger offering of a ram and makes a condition. The גמרא asks whether that condition also covers the chance that the פלגס is a בריה of its own, and the question ends as תיקו. Next, רבי זירא asks a similar question about שיאור, dough that has started to rise but is not fully leavened. Someone vowed to bring תודה loaves of חמץ or of מצה and brought שיאור. After sorting out רבי מאיר's and רבי יהודה's definitions, the question narrows to one case: is רבי יהודה's שיאור a doubt, so it works either way, or a separate kind of thing that works for neither? A challenge from רב הונא forces the case to be narrowed twice, and the question again ends as תיקו. Then a new משנה teaches that פרה אדומה and עגלה ערופה follow opposite rules. A ברייתא explains that the פרה needs שחיטה and the עגלה needs עריפה. The amud ends with a קל וחומר challenge asking why the פרה should not also be valid with עריפה.

steps.title: בר פדא's method: bring and make a condition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its description of בר פדא's view: for a פלגס, one brings the larger offering of a ram and makes a condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: For he says that one brings the offering and makes a condition.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a sentence from before this section: בר פדא says that someone offering a פלגס brings the מנחה and נסכים of a ram and makes a condition. It sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we are unsure whether a פלגס counts as a ram or a lamb, בר פדא solves it by bringing the larger amount. He says: if it is a ram, this is its proper offering; if it is a lamb, the extra is a נדבה. The next step asks how far this condition reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: He brings
He stipulates, makes a condition

phrases.english: As he says: he brings and stipulates.
phrases.notes: 'He' is בר פדא, and he's talking about a פלגס, the in-between animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a statement that began before this section, giving בר פדא's method for a פלגס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a פלגס, one brings the larger ram-offering and makes a condition covering both ram and lamb.

steps.title: Does the condition also cover the possibility that it is a separate creature?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether בר פדא's condition covers only ram or lamb, or also the possibility that the פלגס is its own בריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say that he makes a condition only for ram or lamb, but not for it being a separate creature? Or perhaps he also makes a condition for it being a separate creature, saying: if it is a separate creature, let the whole thing be a gift offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about how wide בר פדא's condition is. Does it only cover ram versus lamb, or also a third option, that the פלגס is a creature of its own?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: בר פדא does not consider the 'separate creature' idea at all, so his condition covers only ram or lamb. Option two: he does consider it, and adds that if it is a בריה, the whole offering becomes a נדבה. The practical difference: under option one, someone who vowed 'a ram or a lamb' could bring a פלגס with a condition and fulfill his vow. Under option two, the doubt remains, so he would not fulfill it.

keyTerms.meaning: A separate creature, a category of its own
A ram
A lamb
A voluntary gift offering
Or perhaps (introduces the second side of a question)

steps.confusionAlert: There are three possibilities here, not two: ram, lamb, or a separate creature. The question is only whether the third one is included in the condition.

phrases.english: Do we say: he stipulates about ram or lamb,
but about a separate creature he does not stipulate,
or perhaps he also stipulates about a separate creature,
saying: if it is a separate creature,
let all of it be a gift offering?
phrases.notes: 'All of it' means the whole נסכים offering he brought, since no part would then be required.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far the condition from step 1 reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether בר פדא's condition also includes the possibility that the פלגס is a בריה in its own right.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves the question as תיקו, unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot settle the question about בר פדא's condition, so it leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since nothing decides it, we do not know whether בר פדא includes the 'separate creature' option. That doubt stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: For בר פדא, a פלגס is handled by bringing a ram's offering with a condition. Whether that condition also covers it being a separate creature is left as תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of step 2 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Unresolved: we do not know whether בר פדא's condition includes the בריה possibility.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks about in-between dough for a thanks offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks: if someone vowed תודה loaves of חמץ or of מצה and brought שיאור, what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asks: one who says, 'I take upon myself to bring loaves of a תודה, of חמץ or of מצה,' and he brought שיאור, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא opens a new question with the same 'in-between' idea, this time about dough. He asks whether שיאור, dough that has begun to rise, works for someone who vowed חמץ or מצה loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תודה comes with both חמץ loaves and מצה loaves. שיאור is in the middle: not fully חמץ and not clearly מצה. The question is whether it counts as one of them, or whether it is its own category like the בריה idea above.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks, raises a question
The loaves that accompany a thanks offering
Leavened bread
Unleavened bread
Dough that has started to rise but is not fully leavened
What is the law?

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira asks:
One who says: 'It is upon me to bring loaves of a thanks offering
of leavened bread or of matza,'
and he brought half-leavened dough, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new but parallel question: in-between dough instead of an in-between animal.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether שיאור fulfills a vow to bring תודה loaves of חמץ or of מצה.

steps.title: Whose definition of שיאור is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which definition of שיאור רבי זירא means, and starts with רבי מאיר's: according to רבי יהודה, that dough is real מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: שיאור according to whom? If it is the שיאור of רבי מאיר, according to רבי יהודה it is full-fledged מצה.
steps.whatsHappening: Before answering, the גמרא asks what exactly רבי זירא means by שיאור, since רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה define it differently. It starts testing the first option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שיאור means the earlier stage that רבי מאיר calls שיאור, then for רבי יהודה it is simply מצה. In that case there is no real question, because it would fulfill a vow for מצה. The גמרא is narrowing down which case could still make רבי זירא's question real.

keyTerms.meaning: Of whom? According to whose opinion?
Full-fledged, proper מצה

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה use the same word שיאור for different stages of rising. The stage רבי מאיר calls שיאור is, for רבי יהודה, not leavened at all.

phrases.english: Half-leavened dough according to whom?
If it is the half-leavened dough of Rabbi Meir,
according to Rabbi Yehuda it is full-fledged matza.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the key term in רבי זירא's question before trying to answer it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which definition of שיאור (רבי מאיר's or רבי יהודה's) רבי זירא's question is about.
steps.kashyaTarget: The meaning of שיאור in רבי זירא's question
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it means רבי מאיר's שיאור, then for רבי יהודה it is simply מצה, so the question would have an obvious answer.

steps.title: Ruling out two more kinds of שיאור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא continues sorting the options. רבי יהודה's שיאור, according to רבי מאיר, is real חמץ. רבי מאיר's own שיאור, according to רבי מאיר, is also חמץ, because he says one gets lashes for eating it on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he means רבי יהודה's kind of שיאור, then according to רבי מאיר it is plain חמץ. And if he means רבי מאיר's kind, according to רבי מאיר, it is also חמץ, since one gets lashes for eating it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still working out which שיאור רבי זירא's question is about. It rules out two more options because in both cases the dough is clearly חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two definitions of שיאור (רבי מאיר's and רבי יהודה's) and two opinions about its law, which gives four combinations. Step 5 showed one combination is clearly מצה. Here two more turn out to be clearly חמץ, so a vow of חמץ loaves is simply fulfilled and there is no question. This leaves only one combination, which the next step takes up.

keyTerms.meaning: It is leavened bread, fully and clearly חמץ.
Gets lashes, the punishment of מלקות.
Since one gets lashes for it. This proves the dough counts as חמץ.

phrases.english: If it is the [שיאור] of Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: שיאור is the stage of dough רבי יהודה has in mind, which is a later stage than רבי מאיר's.

phrases.english: according to Rabbi Meir, it is leavened bread.
And if it is the [שיאור] of Rabbi Meir, according to Rabbi Meir,
since one gets lashes for [eating] it, it is leavened bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר – חָמֵץ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of options begun in Step 5 and rules out two more.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of שיאור רבי זירא's question could be about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In these two combinations the שיאור is clearly חמץ, so they cannot be the case of the question.

steps.title: The real question: is שיאור a doubt or a separate kind of thing?
steps.stepSummary: The only case left is רבי יהודה's שיאור according to רבי יהודה. The גמרא asks whether it is a doubt, so a person fulfills his vow either way, or a separate kind of thing that is neither חמץ nor מצה, so he does not fulfill it.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the question must be about רבי יהודה's שיאור according to רבי יהודה. What is the law? Is it a doubt, so he fulfills his vow whichever way you look at it? Or is it its own kind of thing, so he does not fulfill it?
steps.whatsHappening: After ruling out every other combination, the גמרא states what רבי זירא was really asking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, his own שיאור must be destroyed before פסח, but there are no lashes for eating it. That could be because we are unsure whether it is חמץ, or because it is a third category. If it is a doubt, it is either חמץ or מצה, so it fulfills a vow of either kind. If it is a separate category, it fulfills neither.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt. We don't know which of two things it is.
Whichever way you look at it. Either option leads to the same result.
He fulfills his obligation.

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same pair of sides as the earlier question about the פלגס (a doubt, or its own בריה). Here, though, the item is dough, not an animal.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, מַאי?
phrases.english: Rather, [it is the שיאור] of Rabbi Yehuda according to Rabbi Yehuda. What [is the law]?
Is it a doubt,
and he fulfills [his vow] whichever way you look at it,
or perhaps it is a separate kind of thing,
and he does not fulfill [his vow]?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the other options are ruled out, this states the one case that is left as the true question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהודה's שיאור is a doubt between חמץ and מצה or its own category.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא's question is only about רבי יהודה's שיאור according to רבי יהודה: is it a doubt (it works either way) or a בריה (it works for neither)?

steps.title: Challenge from רב הונא: a doubt would not be enough either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the 'doubt' side. רב הונא says that someone who vows 'תודה loaves' must bring the full תודה with all its loaves, both מצה and חמץ. If he brings שיאור, he cannot know which kind he is still missing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב הונא said that one who says 'I take upon myself תודה loaves' brings a תודה and all its loaves. Since he must bring all the loaves, this man does not know whether the שיאור is חמץ, so that he should bring מצה, or מצה, so that he should bring חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that if שיאור is a doubt, the person is fine 'whichever way you look at it.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא teaches that a vow of תודה loaves obligates the whole set of מצה and חמץ loaves. If one part is brought as שיאור, which is a doubt, he still has to bring the other kind, but he does not know which kind that is. So a doubt does not let him complete his obligation, and the 'מִמָּה נַפְשָׁךְ' reasoning seems not to work.

keyTerms.meaning: It is upon me. The wording of a vow (נדר).
The animal offering together with its full set of loaves.
He became obligated.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Huna say:
One who says: 'It is upon me [to bring] loaves of a thanks offering'
brings a thanks offering and its loaves,
and since he is obligated in a thanks offering and its loaves,
this man does not know
whether it is leavened bread, so that he should bring matza,
or whether it is matza, so that he should bring leavened bread!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'doubt, so it works either way' side of the question in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that if שיאור is a doubt, he fulfills his vow מִמָּה נַפְשָׁךְ.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A vow of תודה loaves requires both מצה and חמץ. A doubtful loaf leaves him not knowing which kind is still missing, so he can never be sure he completed the set.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that even if שיאור is only a doubt, using it may not satisfy an obligation that requires both kinds of loaves.

steps.title: The question is about vowing only the loaves for someone else's offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers רב הונא's challenge. רבי זירא means a case where the person vowed only the loaves, to exempt another person's תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the question is needed where he said: 'I take upon myself the loaves, to exempt so-and-so's תודה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the 'doubt' side by moving רבי זירא's question to a different case. In this case the person did not vow a whole תודה, only the loaves for someone else's תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's problem was that someone who vows a whole תודה must bring every kind of loaf, and שיאור leaves him unsure which kind he is missing. If the person only promised loaves for someone else, he is not obligated in the whole set himself. So the problem seems to go away.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for... (the case is narrowed to a specific situation)
Here: the loaves of the תודה, not the dough portion given to a כהן
To exempt; to cover someone else's obligation
So-and-so; some other person

steps.confusionAlert: חלה here does not mean the piece of dough given to a כהן. It means the loaf part of the תודה.

phrases.english: No, it is needed only
where he said: "It is upon me to bring the loaves
phrases.notes: חלה here means the bread part of the תודה, not the dough given to a כהן.

phrases.english: to exempt the תודה of so-and-so."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of רב הונא from step 8 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי זירא's question was about someone who vowed a whole תודה, which needs every kind of loaf.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is about someone who vowed only loaves to exempt another person's תודה, so he is not obligated in the whole set.

steps.title: The owner still does not know which loaf he is missing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. Even so, the owner of the תודה cannot tell whether the שיאור counts as חמץ or מצה, so he does not know what to add.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, this man does not know: if it is חמץ, he should bring מצה, and if it is מצה, he should bring חמץ!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer in step 9. The person whose תודה was supposed to be exempted still has the same problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner of the תודה needs both מצה and חמץ loaves. If the שיאור is a doubt, he cannot tell which kind it covers, so he must bring both kinds anyway. That means the vow did not exempt him from anything, and the case from step 9 does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end; after all (the problem is still there)
Man; here, the owner of the תודה
So that he should bring

phrases.aramaic: סוֹף סוֹף הָא לָא יָדַע הַאי גַּבְרָא,
phrases.english: Ultimately, this man does not know
whether it is חמץ, so that he should bring מצה,
or whether it is מצה, so that he should bring חמץ!

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף הָא לָא יָדַע הַאי גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case in step 9, where loaves were vowed to exempt someone else's תודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If שיאור is a doubt, the owner still has to bring both kinds himself, so the vow 'to exempt' accomplishes nothing.

steps.title: The question is only whether the vower kept his vow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is where he did not say 'to exempt.' The only question is whether the person who vowed has fulfilled his own vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where he did not say 'to exempt.' Does the man fulfill his vow, or does he not fulfill it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the case one more time and restates רבי זירא's question in its final form.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he never promised to exempt the owner, the owner's problem does not matter to him. The only issue is his own vow to bring חמץ or מצה loaves: does a שיאור loaf count as keeping that promise? This brings back the choice from step 7: a doubt (he fulfills either way) or a separate kind of thing (he does not).

keyTerms.meaning: His vow (literally, 'the hands of his vow')

phrases.english: No, it is needed only where he did not say "to exempt,"
as for the man fulfilling his vow,
does he fulfill it or does he not fulfill it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10 by narrowing the case again.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vow was meant to exempt the owner, so the owner's uncertainty ruined it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow had no 'to exempt' in it, so the question is only about the vower's own obligation.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends רבי זירא's question with תיקו. It is left undecided.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion without an answer. Nobody resolves whether רבי יהודה's שיאור is a doubt or a separate kind of thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means the question is left open. So we do not know whether bringing שיאור loaves fulfills a vow to bring חמץ or מצה loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא's question ends up about one case only: רבי יהודה's שיאור according to רבי יהודה, where the person vowed loaves without saying 'to exempt.' Is it a doubt or a separate kind of thing? The question stays open: תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question as restated in step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether שיאור loaves fulfill a vow of חמץ or מצה loaves is left undecided.

steps.title: New משנה: פרה אדומה and עגלה ערופה are opposites
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that whatever makes a פרה אדומה valid makes an עגלה ערופה invalid, and the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: What is fit for the פרה אדומה is unfit for the עגלה ערופה. What is fit for the עגלה ערופה is unfit for the פרה אדומה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts with a short משנה comparing two special cows. The משנה does not yet explain what kind of 'fitness' it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה states a two-way rule: the two animals work in opposite ways. The ברייתא in the next step will explain what this means.

keyTerms.meaning: The פרה אדומה, the red heifer
The עגלה ערופה, the heifer whose neck is broken
Fit; valid
Unfit; invalid

phrases.english: MISHNA:
That which is fit for the red heifer is unfit for the heifer whose neck is broken;
that which is fit for the heifer whose neck is broken is unfit for the red heifer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ended with תיקו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פרה אדומה and עגלה ערופה follow opposite rules: what is valid for one is invalid for the other.

steps.title: The ברייתא explains: slaughter versus breaking the neck
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the משנה. A פרה אדומה must be done with שחיטה, and an עגלה ערופה must be done with עריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: A פרה אדומה is valid with שחיטה and invalid with עריפה. An עגלה ערופה is valid with עריפה and invalid with שחיטה. So what is fit for the פרה is unfit for the עגלה, and what is fit for the עגלה is unfit for the פרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to explain what the משנה is talking about. The opposite rules are about the way each animal is killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said the two animals are opposites. The ברייתא tells us how: the פרה אדומה needs שחיטה, while the עגלה ערופה needs its neck broken. Then the ברייתא repeats the משנה's words as its conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughter with a knife across the throat
Breaking the back of the neck
It turns out; consequently

steps.whatToRemember: פרה אדומה needs שחיטה, and עגלה ערופה needs עריפה. Using the wrong method makes each one invalid.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
The red heifer, with slaughter, is fit;
with breaking the neck, it is unfit.
The heifer whose neck is broken, with breaking the neck, is fit;
with slaughter, it is unfit.
Consequently, what is fit for the red heifer is unfit for the heifer whose neck is broken;
phrases.notes: Some versions read נמצאת (in round brackets), while the corrected wording is נמצא (in square brackets). Both mean 'it turns out.'

phrases.english: what is fit for the heifer whose neck is broken is unfit for the red heifer.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: פָּרָה בִּשְׁחִיטָה כְּשֵׁרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה in step 13 by naming the method that makes each animal valid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פרה אדומה is valid only with שחיטה, and עגלה ערופה is valid only with עריפה.

steps.title: Why not let the red heifer be valid with breaking the neck?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא with a קל וחומר. The עגלה ערופה is not valid with שחיטה but is valid with עריפה. So the פרה אדומה, which is valid with שחיטה, should certainly also be valid with עריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the פרה אדומה be valid with עריפה, based on a קל וחומר. The עגלה ערופה is not made valid with שחיטה, yet it is made valid with עריפה. The פרה אדומה is made valid with שחיטה. Doesn't it make sense that it should also be made valid with עריפה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא's rule that a פרה אדומה must be done only with שחיטה. It uses a קל וחומר to argue that עריפה should work for the פרה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument treats שחיטה as the stronger way to kill and עריפה as the weaker one. The עגלה ערופה cannot even use the stronger way, yet the weaker way works for it. So the פרה, which can use the stronger way, should surely be allowed to use the weaker way as well.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stronger case: if it is true in the weaker case, it is surely true in the stronger one
Was made valid, was made fit
Isn't it logical? The standard closing words of a קַל וָחוֹמֶר

steps.confusionAlert: Both animals are called a heifer here. In this argument, עגלה means the עגלה ערופה and פרה means the פרה אדומה. Don't mix them up.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this קל וחומר works, it would erase the משנה's rule that whatever makes one of these two animals valid makes the other invalid. So the גמרא will need to find a reason why this argument fails.

phrases.english: And let the red heifer be valid with breaking the neck
by means of a קל וחומר:
If the heifer whose neck is broken, which is not made valid with slaughter,
is made valid with breaking the neck,
then the red heifer, which is made valid with slaughter,
isn't it logical that it is made valid with breaking the neck?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְהֵא פָּרָה כְּשֵׁרָה בַּעֲרִיפָה מִקַּל וְחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא of step 14, which said a פרה אדומה must be done with שחיטה, by arguing that עריפה should also be valid for it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule (step 14) that a פרה אדומה is valid only with שחיטה, and so the משנה's rule (step 13) that what makes one valid makes the other invalid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: the עגלה ערופה cannot use שחיטה but can use עריפה, so the פרה אדומה, which can use שחיטה, should surely be able to use עריפה.
